correctness.rationale: Exact population truncation and tagged-vertex dynamics are proved for all positive tripartite part sizes; the exhaustive size-independent graph has 17,576 profiles and 109,512 occupied tagged states. Functional-graph analysis gives maximum preperiod 9 and periods 1,3,4,6,12, and all tags satisfy T^21=T^9. Canonical recurrent template equality establishes the three exceptional formulas; direct original-vertex enumeration on 322,218 states verifies instances and a sharp 9-step witness. Infinite-family validity comes from the exact factor proof, not extrapolation.

Existing related threshold-two cyclic competition on K_{a,b} (identifier a04efb42-4ecb-4a47-8ad3-9cf987a7e385) has only periods 1,3,4 and entrance time at most 3; a bipartite result does not classify the tripartite period-six or period-twelve regimes.

Existing threshold-one cyclic competition on complete multipartite graphs (identifier 3a5ba3a5-8c93-4c32-97a7-e1597be1b747) has only periods 1,3 and entrance time at most 2. Threshold-one contact is a different update, not a stronger statement about threshold two.

Existing threshold-two Greenberg-Hastings on complete tripartite graphs (identifier 80bbc669-5856-4804-b757-3d8c7adccf7f) has eventual periods 1,3,4,12 and an eleven-step bound, with primitive-twelve count 2 sum J_GH(s) B(other) B(other). That rule advances refractory classes automatically. The new cyclic competition has a primitive-six regime, a nine-step bound, and a distinct twelve-state count exactly three times the corresponding Greenberg-Hastings formula; neither formula implies the other without a rule-changing proof.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The arbitrary-graph theorem is explicitly for one excited neighbour, not two.
